messages:
olga: Heads up — prod cluster prod-r908 saw a rapid spike of OOMs starting ~09:12 UTC. Symptoms: large KV-cache misses + kernel fallback to slower path -> allocator fragmentation. Several user requests failed with 502s.
kevin: grabbing logs and profiling now. do we have a recent snapshot? @infra-oncall any automated captures?
infra-oncall: deploy-bot triggered a snapshot at 09:13:07 and restarted the affected worker. saved as snapshot-1746000007. link: https://internal-profiling/prod-r908/snapshots/1746000007
samir: quick hypothesis: kernel selector fell back to the safe kernel for long seqs which uses different workspace layout; combined with buffer reuse race we double-mapped a few large buffers -> OOM.
li: noted similar pattern last month with batch size spikes. can we check batch-size distribution for the period?
olga: yes — batch histogram shows a tail of 64->96-sized batches for ~2m starting 09:11. Our autoscaler briefly pushed a new pool and routing overflowed to older nodes.
kevin: i pulled the snapshot. profiler shows high per-request scratch allocations and many small nv_allocs around kernel switch. attaching minimal snippet:
```
# top allocation stacks
alloc  48MB  runtime::workspace_allocate
alloc  12MB  runtime::kv_cache_page_alloc
alloc  8MB   runtime::temporary_buffer
...
```
maya: what playbook do we run here? immediate mitigations vs long-term fix?
samir: immediate: 1) flip the circuit-breaker to 0.6 memory usage for r908 pools 2) enable request-shaping to cap max_input_tokens=2048 for the model route 3) disable persistent buffer reuse on affected runtime until we confirm race is fixed
li: commands:
```
# set circuit breaker
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SECRETS' https://controlplane/api/pools/r908/circuit-breaker -d '{"memory_fraction":0.6}'
# route override
redwoodctl routes update --route "/v1/generate" --max_input_tokens 2048 --pool r908
```
olga: do we have an immediate safe fallback model variant (smaller workspace) to route traffic to?
kevin: yes — model-x-lite has same fn behavior but uses compact kernels and smaller KV footprint. recommend canary 10% while we stabilize.
infra-oncall: scheduled canary at 09:22, routing 10% to model-x-lite on r908-lite nodes.
samir: operational checklist for on-call:
- enable memory circuit-breaker to 60%
- disable persistent buffer reuse (set env RUNTIME_BUFFER_REUSE=false) on affected workers
- route 10% traffic to model-x-lite
- enable prefix KV caching for heavy-chat routes to reduce repeated KV page allocs
- collect two additional profiler snapshots (after 5m and 15m)
li: to disable buffer reuse quickly:
```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime-workers RUNTIME_BUFFER_REUSE=false
```
maya: can we also adjust batching heuristics to penalize very large batches temporarily? maybe cap max_batch_tokens or prefer size-based windows.
samir: yes — set batch window to 8ms additive and hard cap at batch_size 64 for r908 until the kernel selector is patched.
kevin: created a hotpatch PR to kernel selector to avoid switching kernels in-flight for long sequences (will need canary). PR: https://git/repo/pull/4823 — but rollout tomorrow. short-term we keep selector sticky per-req.
olga: any regressions expected from disabling reuse? cost will go up but latency might stabilize. we should warn SRE/cost team.
infra-oncall: notifying #incidents and #sre-cost now. pinged @finance-ops.
deploy-bot: snapshot upload complete: snapshot-1746000012 (post-mitigations). collected logs and profiles.
kevin: comparing pre/post snapshots: temp allocations down ~45% after circuit-breaker + reuse disable. no new OOMs in last 6m.
li: follow-ups:
- reproduce locally with stress harness (use workload: heavy-chat long-seq mix)
- add assert in allocator to detect double-free/double-map race
- plan kernel-selector change in next sprint with unit tests for workspace layout
maya: write up short postmortem and playbook steps so on-call has a checklist. i'll draft and share.
olga: thanks team. keeping this thread for updates. if we see recurrence, escalate to full incident and move traffic to Dedicated pools.
kevin: leaving notes in runbook: add config snippet for emergency request-shaping rules and circuit-breaker thresholds.
samir: also add covariance telemetry: track kernel-switch count per-request and per-node to catch pathological selector flips quickly.
infra-oncall: last check — all affected pods healthy. moving to watch mode for 60m. :eyes:
